prerequisites: Knowledge acquired in the second-year course 'Fundamentos de Materiales' (Fundamentals of Materials).
Basic knowledge of chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer science, and language (Spanish).

It is highly recommended that the student has completed and passed the first-year courses 'Física I y II' (Physics I and II), 'Química' (Chemistry), 'Matemáticas I y II' (Mathematics I and II), 'Estadística' (Statistics), and 'Programación' (Programming).

Physics: fundamental and derived magnitudes and their units; error estimation and expression of results according to measurement theory; basic concepts of kinematics, dynamics, mechanics, and hydrodynamics; basic concepts of thermodynamics, electricity, magnetism, and optics; states of matter.

Chemistry: chemical elements of the periodic table; concept of mole, molecule, and molecular weight; basic formulation and nomenclature of organic and inorganic compounds; laws and equations of chemical equilibrium; solid-liquid solutions: concept of concentration and solubility; atomic structure; chemical bonding; crystal order.

Mathematics: calculation of angles, distances, areas, and volumes; representation and analysis of basic mathematical functions (polynomials, logarithms, exponentials, powers, trigonometric...); solving first and second-degree equations and inequalities; trigonometry; vectorial, differential, and integral calculus; linear least squares fitting; coordinate systems; vectors and planes in three-dimensional space; statistics.
Computer Science: spreadsheet; graphical representation of mathematical functions; critical information search on the web.
Language: oral and written expression and reading comprehension in Spanish. Reading comprehension in scientific English.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the chemical composition, structure, and microstructure of metallic, ceramic, polymeric, and composite materials.
Understand the relationship between chemical characteristics and their properties and applications.
Understand the processing techniques of materials and their influence on structure and properties.
Understand the main applications of metallic, ceramic, polymeric, and composite materials.
Understand the testing methods and tools for determining the durability of materials in a given application.
Apply the acquired knowledge to solve problems of material selection and manufacturing, and to estimate the durability of engineering parts under service conditions.

syllabus_topics: Topic 0. Course presentation and its teaching guide
Topic 1. Metals and metallic alloys: processing, properties, and applications
Topic 2. Polymeric materials: structure, processing, and applications
Topic 3. Engineering ceramic materials. Building materials
Topic 4. Composite materials: structure, processing, and applications
Topic 5. Oxidation and corrosion of metals
Topic 6. Durability of ceramics and degradation of polymers
Topic 8. Material selection. Examples of selection
1.1. Synthesis of materials (Practice 1: Synthesis of an advanced ceramic by solid-state reaction OR Practice 2: Synthesis of a polymer and manufacture of a polymeric sheet).
1.2. Quality control in material processing (Practice 3: Determination of the curing cycle of a polyester resin OR Practice 4: Rheological behavior of ceramic mixtures).

1.3. Raw materials and manufacture of composite materials (Practice 5: Characterization of fabrics and mats. Fiber preparation for laminate manufacturing; Practice 6: Manufacturing of fiber-matrix laminate specimens for flexural testing).
1.4. Mechanical testing of materials (Practice 7: The stress-strain curve in a flexural test OR Practice 8: The stress-strain curve in a torsion test).
2. Computer practice: use of the GRANTA EDUPACK database for material selection.
teaching_methods: Participatory lectures (overview of topic content, problem-solving, and exercises)
Final course project (critical information search, analysis, and oral presentation)
Laboratory practices (experimental work, data analysis with error estimation)
Individual resolution of problem sets and exercises
Group analysis and presentation of laboratory data
Group preparation and presentation of a final course project

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and engagement in group classes and seminars (continuous theory assessment)
Computer practice and final course project presentation (continuous theory assessment)
Attendance and engagement in all laboratory sessions (lab practices assessment)
Individual exam on laboratory practice content applying measurement theory (lab practices assessment)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 50% from the final theory-problems exam, 25% from continuous theoretical content assessment, and 25% from laboratory practices assessment. To pass the course, students must obtain a score of 5 out of 10 or higher in each of these three main parts (final exam, continuous theory assessment, and lab practices assessment). In the extraordinary call, students must pass the theoretical content part (75% of the final grade) and the practical content part (25% of the final grade); parts passed in the ordinary call can be carried over. Students eligible for a single final assessment will follow the extraordinary call criteria: a final theory exam (75%) and a final lab exam (25%).
